sonnet.problem: The card writes "spoke with Him there: 'the LORD God of Hosts, the LORD is His name of renown.'" The colon makes the quoted words sound like what Jacob said. In Hosea 12:4-5 the line follows a dash and describes who He is, so the text doesn't say it is Jacob's speech. The card closes a connection the text leaves open.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The true/false statement joins two claims: "maintain love and justice" (true) and "wait on your God only when times get hard" (false). It tests more than one claim.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.

sonnet.problem: The first sentence retells Hosea 12:2 ("He will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds"). Card 8 just tested that fact, so the story card repeats an answer already shown and works as a recap.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The joke "that line has me checking my own counter for crumbs" doesn't connect to "they will surely come to nothing." A reader would not see why crumbs on a counter fit the line, and it sits on a judgment line.
sonnet.rule: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it. / A joke that doesn't make sense is worse than no joke.
